decision.material_delta: Add cellular C2alpha sparing and exposure-matched mitochondrial function to the focused muscle proof; preserve adult-stage and respiratory-function questions as distinct bridges.
decision.reason: New mitochondrial-fusion evidence creates a testable target/isoform hazard. Selective vascular and chronic catalytic-loss evidence prevents assigning combined-deletion injury to exact BLU3797.

findings.title: Class-II PI3K-dependent mitochondrial fusion requires an exposure-linked challenge
findings.decision_delta: Measure cellular C2alpha sparing and useful mitochondrial/contractile function at muscle-effective free exposure.
boundaries: Cardiac injury is from combined C2alpha/C2beta deletion, not selective C2beta inhibition.
Individual C2beta protein depletion fragments mitochondria in transformed cells, so alpha sparing cannot by itself dismiss a beta-related mechanism.
The kinase-dead add-back experiment is under double depletion and does not isolate beta-only catalysis.
Thesis and Science paper share research lineage and are not independent replications.

proof_amendments.action: At force-restoring measured free exposures, assess mitochondrial organization with energetic or contractile-fatigue function in the same qualified muscle system.
proof_amendments.advance: Useful force benefit without corresponding useful-function loss over an interpretable exposure range.
proof_amendments.inconclusive: Morphology-only change, uncertain engagement, high-only exposure effect or an estimate crossing the useful threshold.
proof_amendments.stop_or_redirect: Reproducible functional harm overlapping rescue after appropriate controls and orthogonal attribution.

proof_amendments.action: Resolve cellular C2alpha selectivity rather than inferring it from a biochemical panel.
